violations.why: The ISR can reset v_fjord to 0 after the task stores rand() and before the task reads it, so the task sees 0 rather than its own value.
The ISR can zero v_fjord after the range check on the value read at line 12 and before line 17 reads it again, so the check no longer matches the value used.
The ISR write of 0 can land between the checked read and the increment store, and the store then overwrites it with a stale value.
The increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so the ISR reset can be lost when the task writes back the old value plus 1.
The ISR can overwrite the value stored at line 26 before the task reads v_fjord at line 17.
